section: Solid waste, plastic waste, e-waste, biomedical and construction waste - rules and management
subsections: SBM-Grameen - launch, ministry, Phase II, ODF Plus, toilets

accepted.s: Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen is implemented by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: SBM-Grameen is run by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. The ministry was renamed in June 2019.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority responsible for the programme.
accepted.sec: SBM-Grameen - launch, ministry, Phase II, ODF Plus, toilets

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Phase I of SBM-Grameen:
1. It aimed to construct over 10 crore toilets by 2019-20.
2. It aimed at making all villages open-defecation free.
3. Rural sanitation coverage increased from 39% in 2014 to 100% in 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the targets and reported sanitation-coverage increase under Phase I of SBM-Grameen.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option after checking each numerical and outcome statement.
accepted.sec: SBM-Grameen - launch, ministry, Phase II, ODF Plus, toilets

accepted.s: The second phase of Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen was approved in 2020 and is intended to continue up to:
accepted.x: Phase II of SBM-Grameen was approved in 2020 for implementation up to 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the end year of Phase II from nearby programme periods.
accepted.sec: SBM-Grameen - launch, ministry, Phase II, ODF Plus, toilets

accepted.s: The principal objective of Phase II of SBM-Grameen is to:
o: Replace all rural toilets with urban sewerage systems
Sustain ODF status and make villages ODF Plus through waste management
accepted.x: Phase II focuses on sustaining open-defecation-free status and achieving ODF Plus through solid and liquid waste management.
accepted.tq: Match the programme phase with its distinctive objective rather than its broad sanitation label.
accepted.sec: SBM-Grameen - launch, ministry, Phase II, ODF Plus, toilets

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes an ODF Plus village?
o: A village with only piped drinking-water connections
A village where ODF status is sustained along with management of greywater, faecal sludge and plastic waste
A village with only household toilets and no waste-management facilities
A village where all waste is incinerated
accepted.x: ODF Plus combines sustained ODF status with management of greywater, faecal sludge and plastic waste, along with options such as biogas and composting.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expanded meaning of a familiar sanitation term.
accepted.sec: SBM-Grameen - launch, ministry, Phase II, ODF Plus, toilets

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct progression of ODF Plus levels?
accepted.x: The three progressive ODF Plus levels are Aspiring, Rising and Model.
accepted.tq: Arrange staged classifications in their stated progression.
accepted.sec: SBM-Grameen - launch, ministry, Phase II, ODF Plus, toilets

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The incentive for an Individual Household Latrine under SBM-Grameen is ₹12,000.
2. Greywater management support is ₹280 per capita for villages up to 5,000 population.
3. Greywater management support is ₹660 per capita for villages above 5,000 population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The IHHL incentive is ₹12,000; greywater support is ₹280 per capita in villages up to 5,000 population and ₹660 per capita in larger villages.
accepted.tq: Check each amount and population threshold before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: SBM-Grameen - launch, ministry, Phase II, ODF Plus, toilets

accepted.s: The Rural Sanitation Strategy covering the period 2019–2029 was prepared by the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
accepted.x: The ten-year Rural Sanitation Strategy for 2019–2029 was prepared by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation.
accepted.tq: Identify the department associated with a named strategy.
accepted.sec: SBM-Grameen - launch, ministry, Phase II, ODF Plus, toilets

accepted.s: Clean Andhra Pradesh, popularly known as the CLAP programme, was launched on 2 October 2021 as:
accepted.x: CLAP was launched on 2 October 2021 under the name Jagananna Swachha Sankalpam. Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra is a later state drive launched in January 2025.
accepted.tq: Use the exact official name to distinguish related sanitation initiatives.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following sanitation programmes in chronological order:
A. Total Sanitation Campaign
B. Swachh Bharat Mission
C. Central Rural Sanitation Programme
D. Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan
accepted.x: The correct order is Central Rural Sanitation Programme (1986), Total Sanitation Campaign (1999), Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan (2012), and Swachh Bharat Mission (2014).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest schemes first, then place the middle programmes by year.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. Integrated Low Cost Sanitation
b. Central Rural Sanitation Programme
c. Total Sanitation Campaign
d. Nirmal Gram Puraskar

List-II (Year)
i. 1980–81
ii. 1986
iii. 1999
iv. 2003

Choose the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Integrated Low Cost Sanitation dates to 1980–81, the Central Rural Sanitation Programme to 1986, the Total Sanitation Campaign to 1999 and Nirmal Gram Puraskar to 2003.
accepted.tq: Start with the earliest sure year and verify the remaining chronological pairs.

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its principal focus?
o: Total Sanitation Campaign — only construction of subsidised rural latrines
Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan — introduction of sanitation for the first time in India
Central Rural Sanitation Programme — award for ODF gram panchayats
Integrated Low Cost Sanitation — conversion of dry latrines to pour-flush latrines and liberation of manual scavengers
accepted.x: The Integrated Low Cost Sanitation programme focused on converting dry latrines into pour-flush latrines and freeing manual scavengers. The other options assign incorrect descriptions.
accepted.tq: Detect the swapped programme-focus pair.

accepted.s: Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan, introduced in 2012, was the renamed form of the:
accepted.x: Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan was the renamed Total Sanitation Campaign and followed a saturation approach.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between predecessor programmes with similar sanitation objectives.

accepted.s: Nirmal Gram Puraskar was primarily an award for:
o: Municipal corporations with the highest waste generation
accepted.x: Nirmal Gram Puraskar, introduced in 2003, recognised open-defecation-free gram panchayats.
accepted.tq: Link a named award with its specific recipient category.

accepted.s: GOBARdhan, launched in 2018 under SBM-Grameen, is associated with conversion of cattle dung, agricultural waste and solid waste into:
accepted.x: GOBARdhan promotes conversion of cattle dung, agricultural waste and solid waste into biogas and bio-slurry, supported by a unified portal.
accepted.tq: Identify the input-output relationship in a waste-to-resource initiative.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Swachhata Hi Seva is correct?
o: It is an award given to ODF gram panchayats.
It is a plastic-import restriction introduced in 2018.
It is a ten-year rural sanitation strategy beginning in 2019.
It is a fortnight-long shramdaan campaign conducted every year since 2017.
accepted.x: Swachhata Hi Seva has been observed as a fortnight shramdaan campaign every year since 2017.
accepted.tq: Separate a recurring campaign from strategies, awards and regulatory measures.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Swachh Bharat Diwas is observed on 2 October.
2. The India Sanitation Coalition was launched in 2015 at FICCI.
3. The India Sanitation Coalition is a multi-stakeholder platform.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe Swachh Bharat Diwas and the India Sanitation Coalition.
accepted.tq: Combine date, place and institutional-character facts in one coded question.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT among the identified items covered by India's single-use plastic ban?
accepted.x: Plastic-stemmed earbuds, straws, stirrers and PVC banners below 100 microns are among the identified banned items. Polycarbonate water storage tanks are not listed in this group.
accepted.tq: Find the item outside the specified banned-item list.

accepted.s: Which authorities are primarily responsible for enforcing the identified single-use plastic ban?
o: Only the Ministry of Jal Shakti
SPCBs/PCCs and local bodies, supported by national and state task forces
Only the National Disaster Management Authority
Only municipal corporations in metropolitan cities
accepted.x: Enforcement involves State Pollution Control Boards or Pollution Control Committees and local bodies, along with a National Level Taskforce and State Special Task Forces.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct combination of implementing authorities.

accepted.s: The identified single-use plastic ban covers approximately what proportion of total plastic waste?
accepted.x: The ban covers only about 11% of total plastic waste.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise proportion rather than assuming that the ban covers all plastic waste.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bangladesh — first country to ban thin plastic bags in 2002
China — first country to ban thin plastic bags in 2002
New Zealand — first ban on thin plastic bags in 2002
accepted.x: Bangladesh was the first country to ban thin plastic bags in 2002. China's National Sword Policy began in 2018, while New Zealand's supermarket produce-bag ban was in July 2023.
accepted.tq: Detect swapped countries and years in closely related international measures.

accepted.s: China's National Sword Policy of 2018 and Thailand's 2025 measure primarily restrict:
o: Domestic manufacture of all plastic products
accepted.x: China's National Sword Policy and Thailand's 2025 measure restrict imports of plastic waste.
accepted.tq: Identify the regulated activity rather than the broad environmental theme.

accepted.s: Nurdles are best described as:
o: Secondary microplastics formed only by tyre wear
Primary microplastic pellets generally measuring 1–5 mm
Biodegradable plastic fibres used in clothing
accepted.x: Nurdles are primary microplastic pellets, generally 1–5 mm in size.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a specific microplastic form from its sources and effects.

accepted.s: India's first major nurdle landing was reported in:
o: Kerala, from the MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck
West Bengal, from a fishing vessel
accepted.x: The first major nurdle landing in India occurred in Kerala following the MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck. The nurdles included LDPE and HDPE.
accepted.tq: Combine location, event and source-vessel clues.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about microplastics:
1. FSSAI detected microplastics in all tested sugar and salt samples.
2. Microbeads in cosmetics are prohibited under the Plastic Waste Management Rules.
3. Microplastics in the Sundarbans can drive plastic-degrading enzymes in microbes carrying antimicrobial-resistance genes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The stated responses include the microbead restriction and the National Action Plan for Marine Litter.
accepted.tq: Test findings, regulatory action and ecological consequence together.

accepted.s: Which plastic is commonly used for water and soft-drink bottles and may leach additives when heated?
accepted.x: PET is widely used for water and soft-drink bottles and may leach additives when heated.
accepted.tq: Match an everyday product with its material and hazard.

accepted.s: Polycarbonate containers are associated with the release of which endocrine-disrupting substance?
accepted.x: Polycarbonate hard bottles and containers can release bisphenol A, or BPA, an endocrine disruptor.
accepted.tq: Use the product–additive association to resolve a material question.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: LDPE/HDPE — carry bags and milk bottles
accepted.x: Synthetic rubber is associated with tyres, not drinking-water bottles. LDPE/HDPE, synthetic polymers and cellulose acetate have the associations shown in the other options.
accepted.tq: Find the product-material mismatch among familiar plastic applications.

accepted.s: Tyre-wear microplastics are principally associated with:
accepted.x: Tyres contain synthetic rubber, and their wear is a source of microplastics.
accepted.tq: Link a pollution source to the material from which it is made.

accepted.s: Which standard must compostable plastics meet?
accepted.x: Compostable plastics must meet the IS/ISO 17088 standard.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact technical standard rather than a general environmental certification.

accepted.s: Under the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2024, which of the following is required for makers of biodegradable plastics?
o: Approval only from local village panchayats
Certification by the Central Pollution Control Board
Certification only by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
Registration with the National Disaster Management Authority
accepted.x: The 2024 amendment defined biodegradable plastics and required CPCB certification for their makers.
accepted.tq: Identify the competent certifying authority in a regulatory provision.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about plastic-waste management:
1. Plastic roads are promoted under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016.
2. Energy recovery from plastic waste is promoted under the same framework.
3. Plastic waste can serve as a feedstock for advanced biofuel.
4. Waste-to-oil is an allowed end-of-life route.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe recognised or promoted routes for plastic-waste utilisation and recovery.
accepted.tq: Check whether each listed recovery route belongs to the same regulatory framework.
